Inspect request samples

Up to ten selected requests per minute. Public aliases replace original request and session IDs; prompt text and raw tokens stay in the private dataset. Session aliases are stable within this preview.

Planned offsetRequest aliasSession aliasInputIdeal cachedIdeal uncached

Many long prefixes—not merely many session names

Each sampled rolling minute contains at least 93 distinct exact 16,384-token prefix families and 102–262 sessions. The largest 16K family contributes at most 6.763% of eligible prompt tokens. This analysis covers at least 96.01% of all prompt tokens in each sampled window.

At 32,768 tokens the minimum is 110 families, but worst-window coverage falls to 76.79%; the longer-prefix count must not be read as coverage of every request.

Transparent review of the extra concentration guard

An assistant-added 5% single-session share guard produced 18 warnings. The reviewed engineering cap is 7%; observed maximum is 6.171%. Original warnings and generation settings remain in the private audit. Neither the selected request schedule nor the numerical results changed. This was not a relaxation of a 5% limit requested by Tom.

Why was it “not yet registered/prepared”?

Because we had completed dataset construction and a read-only preview, but had not yet integrated the new pack into Alex. This is a workflow status—not an incompatibility, and not a claim that Alex cannot reuse it.

1. Saved packOriginal request frames + selected replay clockCompleted
2. Catalog entryName, discoverable path, dataset identityNot done at export
3. Prepared profileCorrect tokenizer and token-cache fingerprintNot done at export
4. Faithful live runWarmup barrier, schedule, endpoint checksSeparate validation

The deployed trace-pack loader already accepted the saved files: 32,457 requests and 1,594 sessions including warmup. The selected compressed payloads were copied byte-for-byte and verified after writing. The original dataset was not overwritten.

The source data mount was read-only, so the derived pack was saved separately on writable Replay storage. Saving there alone did not make Alex discover the new directory or create a prepared model-specific profile.

Yes—we can register it for later reuse

The durable deliverable should be a named dataset plus a verified prepared tokenizer profile, not just this documentation page or a browser tab.

  1. Register the exact saved pack. In Alex Replay, open 数据来源 → 扫描目录, enter the derived pack’s directory, then select 扫描数据. The supported scanner accepts an explicit existing directory outside the default scan root. It reads metadata and adds the dataset to the catalog; it does not copy the 2 GB payload or send inference traffic. Verify the new entry points to the derived pack—not its parent corpus—and shows 32,457 requests including warmup. The current basename would produce the generic label “trace-pack”; choose a clear stable final name before preparing, because changing its path later changes identity.
  2. Prepare the derived dataset for GLM-5.3. Alex needs exact local input-token counts and its matching token-cache artifacts. This is offline preparation, not inference load and not warming the model’s KV cache. A structurally valid pack may already be labeled “ready” while the separate tokenizer badge still says “需先 Prepare”; these are different readiness checks.
  3. Reuse the parent’s tokenization safely where supported. The request bodies are unchanged, so existing exact tokens are potentially reusable. But source paths and file statistics, ordered request IDs, and tokenizer/template metadata give this pack a new fingerprint. A valid derived cache must contain the appropriate entries and manifest under that new identity; simply borrowing the old cache key is incorrect. The existing extraction scripts do not yet implement this automatic derivation helper. Otherwise use Alex’s normal preparation path.
  4. Save a replay configuration that preserves the intended experiment. Use timestamp Replay rather than TPM rescheduling. Keep the 100-token output override explicit. Preserve the curated timestamps and cross-session order; do not silently repack the requests into a different schedule.
  5. Validate the run separately. Complete the 100 warmup requests before beginning the measured hour, verify endpoint readiness, and compare actual admissions and cache hits against the offline targets. Stock Replay’s pre-roll does not drain automatically at the measurement boundary. A catalog entry or “prepared” label cannot guarantee prefix readiness or the requested live cache-hit rate.

Registration and normal Prepare send no model requests. Starting warmup or a test is separate. The inspected pack/catalog storage uses a host-backed mount and survives pod recreation with that same backing mount; portability to a different node is not automatic. Persistence must cover the actual pack, the catalog record and prepared cache.

How this workflow was verified

A read-only live catalog check still showed the original five datasets without this subset. The deployed controller, catalog and HTTP-server source files matched the inspected checkout by SHA-256. The scan controller accepts an explicit existing path, and the deployed preparation branch records zero network requests. The UI’s tokenizer-readiness badge is separate from structural dataset readiness. These observations were checked on 2026-09-09; no registration or preparation was performed as part of that inspection.

What preparation cannot guarantee

  • Cache semantics: the audit assumes an initially cold, global, unbounded, input-only prefix cache, 64-token pages and one reserved last input token. Output KV is excluded. Actual finite L1/L2/L3 capacities, eviction, routing and request failures can change hits.
  • Readiness: planned parent/session gaps of at least 5.0065 seconds do not prove completion. The artificial five-minute warmup span is not a completion barrier.
  • Rate semantics: 30M scheduled input TPM is not a guarantee of 30M admitted, completed or GPU-processed TPM. Concurrency backpressure and delayed prerequisites can miss minute quotas; those misses must remain visible.
  • Scheduling: stock TPM mode can change order. Timestamp Replay expresses the curated schedule but still needs validation under backpressure.

Warmup uses 6,350,035 input tokens and 5,359,168 unique modeled prefix-page tokens. It is excluded from the 60 measured minutes and is not a repeated measured-request loop.

Evidence and provenance

Source: the existing 13-hour real-traffic Alex trace from 2026-07-24, with 66,167 requests and 7,820 sessions; exact prepared GLM-5.3 tokens were reused for offline analysis. Filtering excludes unusable token normalizations, inputs above 190,000 tokens and dependent descendants.

Preserved: original request bodies, IDs and within-session source order. Changed: request selection, cross-session interleaving and replay timestamps. The compressed request payload, including warmup, occupies 2.013 GB; indexes are additional.

Download the public scalar audit data: all fixed-minute rows, boundary extrema, prefix-diversity summaries and public sample aliases. It is not the launch dataset and contains no model request payloads.
